title: Sensitivity-tiered Audit Ledger and Rollback Evidence Playbook
author: Elena Kim
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines a standardized approach to: (1) maintain a sensitivity-tiered audit ledger that ties RBAC activations, authorization decisions, and model-serving events to forensic-ready evidence bundles; and (2) collect, package, and preserve rollback evidence when an automated or manual model rollback is triggered. The goal is to ensure regulatory and legal defensibility while minimizing operational load during high-severity incidents.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all Redwood services that perform model serving, routing, and customer-specific inference (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Covers three audit sensitivity tiers: PUBLIC, INTERNAL, and SENSITIVE.
- Integrates with audit logging pipeline, entitlement systems, and the evidence orchestration service (evidence-orch).

Definitions:
- Audit ledger: append-only time-ordered record of authorization and critical model events with contextual pointers to evidence bundles.
- Evidence bundle: a compressed, signed package (ZIP + manifest.json + chain-of-custody) containing logs, snapshots, and attestations required for post-incident review or regulator requests.
- Rollback trigger: any automated safety rollback or operator-initiated model rollback that removes a model variant from serving or pins traffic to an older version.

Sensitivity tiers and retention policy:
- PUBLIC: non-sensitive telemetry and aggregate metrics. Retention: 90 days. Audit ledger entries may include pointers but not raw payloads.
- INTERNAL: operational traces, per-request latency, non-PHI user identifiers. Retention: 2 years. Evidence bundles include anonymized request traces.
- SENSITIVE: customer-provided PII/PHI, contractual data subject to residency restrictions, privileged entitlement changes (role grants/scoped tokens). Retention: per-customer contract + legal minimum (commonly 7 years). Evidence bundles include encrypted raw artifacts and KMS-backed key ids.

Ownership and roles:
- Evidence owner: Security (owned by Elena Kim) — responsible for evidence-orch runbook and forensics packaging templates.
- On-call responder: Eng-SRE (primary) + ModelOps (secondary).
- Legal/Compliance liaison: assigned per-case by the legal team.

Audit ledger schema (summary):
- ledger_id: UUIDv4
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- service: short-name (e.g., runtime-proxy, kv-cache, model-router)
- event_type: AUTHZ_DECISION | MODEL_DEPLOY | MODEL_ROLLBACK | TOKEN_ISSUE | DATA_ACCESS
- actor: principal id (user/service)
- target: resource id (model:version / dataset / route)
- sensitivity_tier: PUBLIC|INTERNAL|SENSITIVE
- evidence_pointer: signed URL or evidence-orch artifact id
- immutable_hash: sha256 of ledger line (for tamper-evidence)

Note: the full schema is stored in the audit-schema registry. Ledger entries must be written as atomic transactions to the ledger service using the ledger-write API.

Operational runbook: immediate actions on rollback trigger (short checklist):
1) Triage and classify the rollback cause and sensitivity tier. If the rollback touches SENSITIVE data paths, immediately mark the case as FACTORY (highest attention) and notify Legal + Customer Success.
2) Capture live traces using trace-grab with the request filter derived from the rollback time window (recommended +/- 5 minutes). Command example:
   - ./trace-grab --service runtime-proxy --start "2026-11-02T10:23:00Z" --end "2026-11-02T10:33:00Z" --trace-filter "model_id:prod-lex-1 AND route:customer-42" --output /tmp/evidence/traces.json
3) Freeze the ledger segment for the rollback epoch (write a ledger tombstone entry to prevent background compaction).
4) Invoke evidence-orch to assemble the bundle: 
   - /usr/local/bin/evidence-orch assemble --case-id CASE-<YYYYMMDD>-<N> --sensitivity SENSITIVE --inputs /tmp/evidence/traces.json,/var/log/runtime-proxy.log,/etc/model-manifest/prod-lex-1.json --kms-key alias/redwood-evidence --output /evidence/cases/CASE-<id>.zip
5) Generate chain-of-custody manifest (manifest.json) containing hashes, signer, signer-key-id, and a short human summary.
6) Store evidence bundle in restricted evidence-bucket with server-side encryption and retention lock according to tier. Ledger entry must reference the stored artifact id.
7) Update the incident tracker with links to the ledger entry and evidence bundle; set incident priority based on sensitivity tier and affected customer SLAs.

Evidence bundle composition requirements (by sensitivity tier):
- PUBLIC: summary.json (event summary), metrics snapshot (prometheus-export), and anonymized route counts.
- INTERNAL: everything from PUBLIC + sampling of request traces (up to 1,000 requests), runtime host metadata (ami, kernel), and model manifest snapshot.
- SENSITIVE: everything from INTERNAL + full request payloads for the affected window, authz decision logs, full model input/output pairs for the window, KMS key ids used, and signed attestations from responsible owners.

Packaging manifest example (manifest.json) (single-line for ledger storage):
{
  "case_id": "CASE-20261102-01",
  "created_by": "oncall@eng-sre.redwood.com",
  "sensitivity": "SENSITIVE",
  "parts": ["traces.json","runtime-proxy.log","model-manifest.json","authz.log"],
  "hash": "sha256:<hex>",
  "signed_by": "evidence-orch@redwood.com",
  "signature_key": "kms://alias/redwood-evidence"
}

Tamper-evidence and verification:
- All ledger writes compute immutable_hash = sha256(ledger_line_json || previous_hash). The ledger service exposes ledger_verify --entry-id <id> to recompute the chain and verify integrity.
- Evidence bundles must include a detached signature (RFC7515) using a KMS-backed key. Verification steps are documented in the evidence verification guide.

Audit logging and RBAC integration points:
- Authorization decision events must be emitted to authz-event-stream with the following minimal fields: principal, action, resource, decision, reason_code, token_id, timestamp.
- A dedicated consumer (evidence-orch) subscribes to authz-event-stream and correlates decisions with request traces via token_id or trace_id.

Automation: retention and deltas
- Retention enforcement is automated: evidence-orch will set object lifecycle policies and legal holds according to sensitivity. A retention manifest is attached to each stored bundle.
- When performing retention reductions (e.g., archive from 7 years to 3 years under a legal exception), a signed retention-decision record must be appended to the ledger and to the case manifest.

Controller-level configuration table (example values):
| setting_key | default | allowed_values | owner |
| ledger_write_timeout | 2000ms | 500ms-10000ms | eng-infra |
| evidence_orch_max_bundle_size | 2GB | 100MB-10GB | security |
| sensitivity_default | INTERNAL | PUBLIC|INTERNAL|SENSITIVE | product |
| retention_archive_class | glacier | glacier|nearline|hot | finance |
Post-incident evidence review checklist (for SENSITIVE cases):
1) Evidence bundle integrity verification using ledger_verify and signature verification.
2) Cross-check authz-event-stream against identity provider (IdP) issuance logs for token provenance.
3) Confirm KMS usage (key ids, rotation state) and attach KMS audit records.
4) Produce a short executive summary and attach to incident record; include customer impact, corrective actions, and retention decision.
5) Formalize follow-up actions: compensating controls, policy changes, and timeline for re-ingress testing.

Examples and snippets:
- Example ledger-write (curl):
  curl -X POST https://ledger.internal.redwood/api/v1/entries \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEDGER_API_TOKEN" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"service":"runtime-proxy","event_type":"MODEL_ROLLBACK","actor":"ops@redwood.com","target":"model:prod-lex-1","sensitivity_tier":"SENSITIVE","evidence_pointer":"evidence:CASE-20261102-01"}'

- Example evidence-orch verification command:
  evidence-orch verify --bundle /evidence/cases/CASE-20261102-01.zip --manifest manifest.json --kms-verify-key alias/redwood-evidence

Governance and risk exceptions:
- Any deviation from standard retention (shorter or longer) requires an Authorization Change Request (ACR) submitted to Risk Board with: rationale, legal approval, compensating encrypted backups, and a signed ledger entry with approver identity.
- Temporary access to SENSITIVE bundles for debugging: must be requested via the privileged-access flow, with Just-In-Time (JIT) activation, multifactor approval, and an automated evidence snapshot recorded by evidence-orch.

Metrics and SLOs for the playbook:
- Evidence bundle assembly latency: P90 <= 15 minutes for INTERNAL, <= 45 minutes for SENSITIVE (SLO).
- Ledger write durability: 5 9s for writes (SLA target).
- Verification turnaround: time to verify a bundle end-to-end <= 4 hours (target for high-priority incidents).

Appendix A — Quick troubleshooting steps:
- If evidence-orch fails to sign: check KMS key quotas and rotation status (CLI: aws kms describe-key --key-id <id>), and verify that evidence-orch has kms:Sign permission.
- If trace-grab returns empty: confirm the trace sampling rate and check router-level sampling override. Increase sampling temporarily under oncall supervision and document the change in the ledger.
